Package com.openvireo.core.hosts

Class UrlConnectionTransport

java.lang.Object
com.openvireo.core.hosts.UrlConnectionTransport
All Implemented Interfaces:
HttpTransport
public final class UrlConnectionTransport extends Object implements HttpTransport
An
invalid reference 
HttpTransport
over HttpURLConnection, run on dispatcher (Dispatchers.IO). It works on the JVM and on Android (where HttpURLConnection is OkHttp underneath); on the JVM prefer JavaNetHttpTransport.

As ov_core::host::HttpTransport requires: - No redirects: instanceFollowRedirects = false, so a 3xx comes back as a response and the core refuses it. - Any status is a response: 4xx/5xx bodies are read from errorStream, not thrown. - Headers: the request's headers, in order, plus what the platform always adds (User-Agent, Host, Content-Length, Accept-Encoding on Android). Header values may be bearer tokens and are never logged. - Errors: no network, DNS failure or connection refused → TransportException.Offline, a timeout → Timeout, TLS → Tls, anything else → Other; cancelling the calling coroutine disconnects the request. - Cookies: none are added unless the app installed a process-wide CookieHandler (CookieHandler.setDefault), which HttpURLConnection always consults. Don't install one in a process that uses this transport, or use JavaNetHttpTransport. - PATCH: the JVM's own HttpURLConnection can't send it (Android's can); such a request fails with TransportException.Other. The core uses PATCH for org, vault and service-account renames.

connectTimeoutMs bounds connecting; readTimeoutMs bounds each read of send (streams wait without a read timeout, since server-sent events can be quiet for a long time).
